episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Body Piercing Artist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Reading the Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive in the shop trailer and spread the prints across the table. You trace the dimensions and part locations with your finger. You mark where each section lines up before you touch any steel.

episodes.title: Fitting the Big Vessel
episodes.text: You walk into the on-site fabrication shop to the laid-out vessel sections. You lift and set the large pieces together for a test fit. You check the seams and alignment before it goes to installation.

episodes.title: Checking the Old Boiler
episodes.text: You meet the operator by the boiler that has been losing pressure.

choice.prompt: You see a damp seam and a worn valve nearby. Which do you examine first?

options.label: Start with the damp seam
options.outcome: You clean the seam and find the active leak. You mark it for repair.

options.label: Start with the worn valve
options.outcome: You check the valve and find it is sound. You go back to the seam next.

chat.text: It has been hissing near the back seam since last night.
Can you take a look for leaks or weak spots?

episodes.title: Checking Tubes and Valves
episodes.text: You sit at the rack of tubes, fittings, and valves after lunch. You look over each piece for defects in the same way. Same checks as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pressure Test Drops
episodes.text: You hook up the gauge and bring the vessel up to test pressure. The needle falls and you hear air escaping at a joint. You hold the test and look for the source.

choice.prompt: The pressure is falling during the test. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the test and isolate pressure
options.outcome: You vent the vessel down safely. You mark the leaking joint to examine.

options.label: Keep watching the gauge a minute
options.outcome: You watch the needle drop further. You shut the test down and mark the joint.

episodes.title: Final Look Over
episodes.text: You walk the assembled vessel one more time at the end of the day. You look at the tubes, fittings, and controls for anything missed. You note one small defect to fix in the morning.

trial.title: Find the defect first
trial.scenario: You inspect the assembled vessel. One tube shows a leak stain, one fitting is dusty but sound, and one valve handle is stiff but holding.
options: The tube with the leak stain
The dusty fitting
The stiff valve handle
trial.explain: The leaking tube is the defect that needs repair first.

episodes.title: Opening the Ledgers
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and wake your computer. You open the accounting software and pull up today's files. You record new information and save it where you can find it again.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You sit with figures, postings, and documents. You check each entry for correct codes and math. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Running Payroll
episodes.text: You pull up payroll information on your computer. You enter hours and check the totals before you process them. One person's hours look short for the week.

choice.prompt: The payroll total looks short for one person. What do you do before you process it?

options.label: Process it as entered
options.outcome: You process payroll as entered. The short hours go through and you note it to fix next cycle.

options.label: Pause and recheck the entry
options.outcome: You pause payroll and recheck the hours against the source. You find the typo and correct it before processing.

episodes.title: Counting the Deposit
episodes.text: You gather the sales data from the cashiers. You verify the receipts and balance them on your screen. You stack the cash and checks to send to the bank.

trial.title: Put the deposit in order
items: Send cash, checks, and other payment to the bank
Compile data from cashiers
Balance the receipts
Verify the receipts
trial.explain: You compile first, then verify and balance, then send the deposit.

episodes.title: Deposit Will Not Balance
episodes.text: You compare the cashiers receipts to the cash in front of you. The totals do not match.

choice.prompt: The receipts and the cash do not match. What do you do now?

options.label: Recheck figures and postings
options.outcome: You recheck the figures, postings, and documents line by line. You find the wrong code and fix the math.

options.label: Send it to the bank anyway
options.outcome: You send the unbalanced deposit to the bank. The bank flags the difference and you have to fix it tomorrow.

chat.text: My drawer is ten dollars short, what should I do?
I counted twice and checked my receipts.

episodes.title: End of Day Rules
episodes.text: You sit with today's work still open. You check it against federal, state, and company policies and procedures. You fix one code so the file follows the rules.

episodes.title: Morning numbers check
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open your laptop. You pull up yesterday's data on customer ages, needs, and buying habits. You sit and look for patterns in who is buying and who is not.

episodes.title: Talking through the survey
episodes.text: You join a video call to plan consumer research with the marketing team.

choice.prompt: The team is waiting on you to decide how to get better consumer opinions.

options.label: Shorten the survey and retest it
options.outcome: You cut the extra questions and test the shorter version. More people finish it and the answers are clearer to read.

options.label: Keep the long survey running
options.outcome: You leave the survey as it is for another week. You keep getting half-finished answers that are hard to use.

chat.text: The last opinion poll felt too long. People quit halfway.
We still need clear answers on product demand. What should we change?

episodes.title: Checking new answers
episodes.text: You open the same questionnaire inbox you checked yesterday. You scroll through the new responses and flag the blank ones. Tomorrow you will do this again.

episodes.title: Satisfaction scores review
episodes.text: You sit down with the latest customer and employee satisfaction results. You compare this month to last month line by line. You note where satisfaction held steady and where it slipped.

episodes.title: Survey problem surfaces
episodes.text: You look at the morning poll results and something is off. Only a few surveys came back and many answers are blank. You realize the collection method is not working.

choice.prompt: You have to decide what to do about the broken data collection.

options.label: Pause and fix the method now
options.outcome: You stop the current survey and fix the unclear questions. You lose a day of answers but the next batch is usable.

options.label: Keep collecting and hope it improves
options.outcome: You let the survey keep running as it is. You end the day with a thin set of answers you cannot trust.

options.label: Pull existing data instead
options.outcome: You set the faulty survey aside and pull past data you already have. You have something to work with while you fix the new poll.

episodes.title: Turning findings into report
episodes.text: You open a blank report to share what you found today. You turn the data into simple charts. You write the findings in plain words under each chart.

trial.title: Put the report together
items: Write the findings in plain written text
Look over the collected customer data
Share the finished report of findings
Make simple charts that show the data
trial.explain: You look at the data first, then chart it, then explain it in words.

episodes.title: Marking the First Lines
episodes.text: You arrive and set your tools by the foundation. You measure out from the reference points and mark guidelines for the wall. You hang your plumb bob and check with your level.

episodes.title: Building Up the Corners
episodes.text: You start on the corners before the middle. You get the corner pole ready and bring bricks to the corner spot. You work the first bricks into place to start the lead.

choice.prompt: The corner needs to go up plumb. How do you start it?

options.label: Fasten the corner pole in plumb position
options.outcome: You clamp the pole plumb and run your line from it. You lay each course to the line as you fill toward the middle.

options.label: Build a corner pyramid of bricks
options.outcome: You lay up a stepped pyramid at the corner and check it plumb. You stretch your line from the pyramid to guide the courses between corners.

episodes.title: Spreading Mortar Again
episodes.text: You scoop mortar and spread it over the work surface. You smooth it out and set the next brick. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cutting Bricks to Fit
episodes.text: You measure a gap that needs a short piece. You mark a brick for cutting and pick up your hammer. The first cut snaps uneven and the piece will not sit flat.

choice.prompt: The cut piece is jagged and too rough to lay. What do you do?

options.label: Cut a new brick to size with the power saw
options.outcome: You measure and mark a fresh brick and make a clean saw cut. You test the piece in the gap and it sits level.

options.label: Trim the broken piece with trowel edge and hammer
options.outcome: You chip the rough edge down to size with your trowel and hammer. You check the fit and set the smaller piece into mortar.

episodes.title: Checking Each Course Level
episodes.text: You step back and count the courses laid so far. You figure the next angles and check vertical and horizontal alignment. You adjust the line from corner to corner before you lay on.

trial.title: Spot the alignment problem
trial.scenario: You sight down the new course. The left end rides above the line, the middle joints look even, and the corner brick leans out of plumb.
options: The corner brick that is out of plumb
The middle joints that look even
The line stretched tight between corners
trial.explain: You fix the out-of-plumb corner first because the line and courses follow it.

episodes.title: Smoothing the Last Joints
episodes.text: You pick up your trowel for the last stretch of wall. You apply mortar where the joints are thin and smooth over the surface. You look down the face and wipe the extra clean.

episodes.title: Morning Bus Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the lot before the sun is up. You walk around your bus with a checklist. You check tires, brakes, lights, wipers, oil, fuel, and water.

trial.title: Spot the fault
trial.scenario: You test the lights and walk to the back. The left brake light glows red. The right brake light stays dark.
options: Right brake light is out
Tires look low
Fuel is low
trial.explain: You report a light that does not come on because lights must work before you drive.

episodes.title: First Morning Pickups
episodes.text: You pull out on your neighborhood route on strict time. You stop at each scheduled corner and open the door. You watch the clock as students climb on.

choice.prompt: You are two minutes behind and more kids wait ahead. What do you do?

options.label: Stay on route and drive safely
options.outcome: You stay late by a few minutes but keep to the stops and speed limit. Dispatch hears you were late.

options.label: Skip a stop to catch up
options.outcome: You save time but leave kids waiting at their scheduled stop. You have to radio for help for them.

episodes.title: Same Streets Again
episodes.text: You drive the same streets again. You stop at the same corners at the same times. You wait, you open the doors, you close them. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Watching Kids Cross
episodes.text: You stop with flashers on at the school zone. You keep students seated until the bus is fully stopped. You watch them step off and cross in front where you can see them.

episodes.title: Brake Light Fails
episodes.text: You are mid-route when the dash warning comes on for a brake light.

choice.prompt: The brake light is out with students on board. What do you do?

options.label: Pull over safe and report it
options.outcome: You stop in a safe lot and call in the bad brake light. A spare bus is sent to finish the route.

options.label: Keep driving to stay on time
options.outcome: You finish the stops on time but drive without a working brake light. The shop flags the safety risk.

options.label: Check lights then decide
options.outcome: You park, check the rear lights yourself, and confirm the fault. You report exactly what you see to the shop.

chat.text: Got your warning light ping. Where are you parked?
Can you stay put and keep the kids on board?
Tell me what the back lights show.

episodes.title: Writing Up Repair
episodes.text: You park back at the lot after drop-offs. You sit down with the defect form. You write up the brake light and fuel level for the shop.

episodes.title: Planning the Study
episodes.text: You sit down and lay out the work problem in front of you. You list what you need to learn about communications and information flow. You make a simple plan for how you will study it.

episodes.title: Asking How Work Flows
episodes.text: You call staff to gather how the current procedure really works.

choice.prompt: They describe the problem two different ways. What do you ask next?

options.label: Ask them to walk through yesterday step by step
options.outcome: They walk you through each handoff. You write down where the numbers stop.

options.label: Move on to keep the call short
options.outcome: The call ends on time. You are missing details you will need later.

chat.text: We still pass the inventory numbers by hand at the end of the day.
Sometimes they get lost before the next shift sees them.
It slows down the cost check too.

episodes.title: Sorting the Notes
episodes.text: You file the notes on problems and procedures into the same folders. You label and stack them the same way as yesterday. Nothing new happens. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Finding the Pattern
episodes.text: You spread out the gathered information on problems and procedures. You compare what repeats and what does not. You start shaping a solution and one alternative way to proceed.

trial.title: Pick what matters first
trial.scenario: You review notes on communications, information flow, and inventory control. Information flow shows the same delay every day. The other notes show normal counts and one small typo.
options: The repeated delay in information flow
The one small typo
The normal inventory counts
trial.explain: You start with the problem that repeats and blocks the work.

episodes.title: New System Stalls
episodes.text: You join a call because the newly implemented procedure is not functioning smoothly. The people concerned are waiting to talk it through.

choice.prompt: The new procedure is stuck and the team is split. What do you do?

options.label: Confer now on what broke
options.outcome: You stay on the call and list what worked and what did not. You agree on a small fix to try this afternoon.

options.label: Tell them to wait for your report
options.outcome: They stay split between old and new ways for another day. You gather notes to address it later.

options.label: Roll back to the old procedure
options.outcome: Work moves again for today. You will need to revisit the new system tomorrow.

chat.text: We followed the new steps this morning and it jammed.
Half the team went back to the old way to keep up.
Can you help us get it working again?

episodes.title: Writing It Down
episodes.text: You sit back down and document what the study found. You write your recommendations for the system and procedure change in plain order. You save it ready for implementation.

episodes.title: Morning Meat Delivery
episodes.text: You arrive before the shop opens and unlock the back door. The delivery driver wheels in boxes of beef and poultry. You start checking each box before you put anything away, and one box feels warm.

choice.prompt: One box feels warm and the meat inside looks dull. What do you do now?

options.label: Set it aside and check it closely
options.outcome: You keep it out of the cooler and look at the color and smell. You keep the rest of the good delivery moving into storage.

options.label: Put it away with the rest
options.outcome: You stack it in the cooler with the other boxes. You worry about it later when you pull meat for the counter.

episodes.title: Wrapping Morning Cuts
episodes.text: You sit down at the back table with trays of cut meat. You wrap each cut tight, weigh it, add the label, and stick on the price. You stack the finished trays for the counter.

trial.title: Price a tray correctly
items: Price the tray
Wrap the cut
Label the tray
Weigh the tray
trial.explain: You wrap first, then weigh, label, and price so the tag matches what is in the tray.

episodes.title: Filling The Display
episodes.text: You carry the finished trays out front to the cold case. You arrange the cuts in neat rows so shoppers can see them. You turn a few trays forward to look tidy.

episodes.title: Weighing And Wrapping
episodes.text: You stand at the scale and wrap more cuts. You weigh, label, and price one tray after another. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Special Cut Request
episodes.text: A regular stops at the counter and asks for a special cut for dinner tonight.

choice.prompt: The request is a little vague on thickness. What do you do?

options.label: Cut it as you think they mean
options.outcome: You trim and cut to what you think they want. You show them the first piece before you finish the rest.

options.label: Ask them to show thickness
options.outcome: You hold up your fingers and ask how thick. They point, and you cut to match that.

options.label: Cut the standard size
options.outcome: You cut your normal size and wrap it. They take it but say they wanted it thinner.

chat.text: Can you cut this a little thinner than usual?
I need enough for four people.
And can you trim most of the fat off?

episodes.title: Afternoon Trimming Work
episodes.text: You go back to the cutting table for the afternoon meat. You trim fat, bone a shoulder, and tie a roast with string. You grind a tray for the case.

episodes.title: Reading Today's Blueprint
episodes.text: You arrive and hang up your jacket. You sit down with the shop drawing for a set of cabinets. You work out the sizes to build and the order you will shape and join them.

episodes.title: Marking Lumber Parts
episodes.text: You lay out the lumber stock on the bench. You follow the blueprint and measure each cabinet part. You mark the dimensions on the wood for a tight fit.

trial.title: Mark parts in order
items: Mark the cut lines on the lumber stock
Check the blueprint for the part dimensions
Measure the lumber stock with your tape
Compare your marks against the blueprint before cutting
trial.explain: You read the blueprint first, then measure, mark, and check before you cut.

episodes.title: Cutting Cabinet Sides
episodes.text: You set up the power saw for the first cuts. You feed the woodstock through and shape the cabinet sides. You pause when the edge looks a little rough.

choice.prompt: The saw edge looks a little rough. What do you do now?

options.label: Stop and reset the saw
options.outcome: You stop the saw and reset the fence. The next cuts come out clean.

options.label: Keep cutting the rest
options.outcome: You keep feeding stock through. You end up with more edges to fix later.

episodes.title: Checking Every Fit
episodes.text: You sit with a pile of cut pieces. You check each one against the specs for size and fit. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Assembling With Help
episodes.text: You and your coworker lift the cabinet sides into place. You start fitting the parts together.

chat.text: Hold your side steady while I line this up?
This joint feels tight. Want to tap it in together?

episodes.title: Drawer That Won't Fit
episodes.text: You slide a drawer front into the cabinet opening. It sticks and sits crooked in the frame. You measure it and see it does not meet the specs.

choice.prompt: The drawer front does not fit the opening. What do you do?

options.label: Re-measure and trim it
options.outcome: You mark the tight spot and trim it down. The front slides in and sits flush.

options.label: Force it into place
options.outcome: You push it hard into the opening. It wedges and the edge splits a little.

episodes.title: Morning Work Orders
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at the desk. You read through today's work orders one by one. You stack them in order for inspections and brake work.

episodes.title: Checking For Damage
episodes.text: You walk slowly around the sedan in the lot. You look close at the bumpers, doors, and panels for damage. You write down each dent and scratch so repairs can be made.

choice.prompt: You find a long scrape on the rear door. What do you do now?

options.label: Write it down in your findings now
options.outcome: You add the scrape to your notes with its location and size. It goes on the repair list with the rest.

options.label: Leave it off and keep inspecting
options.outcome: You keep walking around the car. The scrape stays unrecorded and no repair gets planned for it.

episodes.title: Test Drive Loop
episodes.text: You take the car out for a test drive around the block. You come back and hook up the compression gauge and diagnostic device. You check the readings on components and systems.

trial.title: Spot the fault first
trial.scenario: You are test driving and checking systems with the diagnostic device. The steering feels normal and lights all work. The brake pedal sinks low and braking feels weak.
options: Brake system needs attention first
Steering system needs attention first
Lights need attention first
trial.explain: The low pedal and weak stopping point to the brakes as the first problem.

episodes.title: Brake Pads Again
episodes.text: You get back to repairing and adjusting brakes after lunch. You reline the same kind of pads the same way as yesterday. You finish, then you start the next car the same way.

episodes.title: Brakes Still Soft
episodes.text: You test the repaired brake system and the pedal still feels soft. You pull the car back in to check it again.

choice.prompt: The repaired brakes still do not feel right on the test. What do you do?

options.label: Test and adjust the system again now
options.outcome: You run the test again and keep adjusting the brakes. You get the pedal feel closer to spec before the day ends.

options.label: Stop testing and move to the next order
options.outcome: You park the car and pick up the next work order. The soft pedal is still there waiting for tomorrow.

options.label: Ask your supervisor to review it with you
options.outcome: You go over the work order and the test with your supervisor. You both look at the brakes together and decide the next adjustment.

chat.text: How did the test feel?
That pedal should be firm by now.
Walk me through what you adjusted.

episodes.title: Fine Tuning Systems
episodes.text: You sit in the last car with your gauge set nearby. You test the repaired system and make small adjustments. You test again until it meets the performance specification.

episodes.title: Calming First Patient
episodes.text: You walk the morning patient to the testing room. She looks nervous about the wires.

choice.prompt: She holds her coat tight and will not sit down. How do you explain the EKG?

options.label: Explain each step slowly and ask her to sit
options.outcome: You tell her what each wire does. She sits down and lets you start.

options.label: Tell her it will be quick and start placing leads
options.outcome: You move fast to get it done. She stays tense through the whole tracing.

chat.text: Will this hurt? I am scared.
You explain it to her? She needs you.

episodes.title: Morning Heart Tracing
episodes.text: You bring in the next patient for an EKG. You place the leads and start the recorder. You watch the line move and save the tracing.

episodes.title: Watching Blood Flow
episodes.text: You sit at the ultrasound screen again. You watch the display and listen for the signal tone. You write down blood pressure and limb changes. Same screen, same notes as yesterday.

episodes.title: Checking Echo Numbers
episodes.text: You pull up the echocardiogram measurements. You compare wall thickness and chamber size to the standard norms. You mark one chamber that looks too large.

trial.title: Spot the Problem
trial.scenario: You compare the echo numbers to the standard chart. One chamber measures much larger than normal. One wall measures only a little thicker than normal.
options: The much larger chamber
The slightly thicker wall
Both look fine
trial.explain: The large difference from the normal size flags the abnormality first.

episodes.title: Holding The Sterile Field
episodes.text: You stand in the procedure room during a heart case. You keep your hands and tools inside the sterile area. Then your sleeve brushes the edge of the drape.

choice.prompt: No one else saw the brush. What do you do about the sterile field?

options.label: Stop and tell the team you need to change
options.outcome: You step back and replace the glove and sleeve. The case pauses a minute, then goes on clean.

options.label: Keep working and say nothing
options.outcome: You keep your place at the table. The field may no longer be sterile for the patient.

episodes.title: Afternoon Stress Test
episodes.text: You set up the stress test bike and heart monitor. You stay beside the patient while he pedals. You record his cardiac activity as the pace picks up.

episodes.title: Reading the Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with the blueprints at the work table. You study the sketches and check the dimensions and materials required. You lay out today's work in order.

episodes.title: Marking Cut Lines
episodes.text: You set the boards on the sawhorses and pick up your ruler. You measure each length and mark the cutting lines with pencil and chalk. You check the marks against the plan once more.

trial.title: Which Needs Attention?
trial.scenario: You check three marked boards against the blueprint. Two cutting lines match the dimensions. One line sits a half-inch past its mark.
options: The board with the line past its mark
A board with a correct mark
Your pencil lying on the bench
trial.explain: You fix the wrong mark before cutting anything.

episodes.title: Cutting the Boards
episodes.text: You carry the marked boards to the power saw. You cut them to the specified measurements and stack the pieces in order. One piece comes out a little long and will not sit flush.

choice.prompt: The long piece will not sit flush. What do you do?

options.label: Measure again and trim it
options.outcome: You remeasure, make a second cut, and the piece fits the layout.

options.label: Leave it long and keep going
options.outcome: You keep building, and the joint stays gapped and uneven.

episodes.title: Sweeping the Shop
episodes.text: You sweep sawdust and offcuts into a pile. You stack the scrap and wipe down the benches. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Building the Frame
episodes.text: You and a coworker start assembling the framework on the floor.

chat.text: Can you hold this upright while I line it up?
Wood screws for this joint?
Ready? I will drive them in now.

episodes.title: Cords Underfoot
episodes.text: You walk back to the saw and see cords and offcuts across the walkway. Sawdust is building up thick near your feet. Someone could trip or slip here.

choice.prompt: You need to make the next cut. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop and clear the walkway
options.outcome: You move the cords, sweep the dust, and the path is safe to walk.

options.label: Step over it and keep cutting
options.outcome: You keep working around the mess and the trip risk stays.

options.label: Quick sweep around the saw only
options.outcome: You clear a small spot, but the cords are still across the path.

episodes.title: Morning Sanitation Log
episodes.text: You arrive early and unlock the small office. You pull out the sanitation binder. You check yesterday's entries and sign today's sheet.

episodes.title: First Guests Arrive
episodes.text: You stand by the door as lunch guests come in. You greet each group and walk them to their tables. You hand out menus and wine lists.

choice.prompt: Two groups arrive at the same time and only one open table is ready. What do you do?

options.label: Seat one group now and ask the other to wait a moment
options.outcome: You escort the first group to their seats and give them menus. You tell the second group the wait is short and seat them next.

options.label: Try to squeeze both groups at the one table
options.outcome: Both groups feel crowded and rushed. You end up moving one group again once another table opens.

episodes.title: Counting Cash
episodes.text: You sit at the back table with the cash drawer. You count the bills and coins the same way as yesterday. You stack the receipts and close the deposit bag. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Setting Service Rules
episodes.text: You gather the staff before dinner service. You go over how to greet and serve each table. You remind everyone what good service looks like.

trial.title: Hold the standard
trial.says: Do we really have to do the greeting the same way every time?
options: Yes, we keep the same standard for every guest so service stays steady.
Just skip it when you are busy, no one will notice.
Do it your own way tonight and we will see what happens.
trial.explain: Keeping the same standard keeps personnel performance and customer service consistent.

episodes.title: Watching the Bar
episodes.text: You stand where you can see the bar and the tables. You notice one table getting loud after another round.

choice.prompt: The corner table is pushing for more drinks past the limit. What do you do?

options.label: Stop service to that table and back up your staff
options.outcome: You tell the staff no more liquor for that table. The guests complain, then settle and stay seated.

options.label: Let the staff serve one more round to keep them happy
options.outcome: The staff pours again and the table gets louder. You have to step in and end service anyway.

options.label: Have staff check IDs again and slow down service
options.outcome: You pause new drinks while IDs are checked. The table waits and the mood cools down.

chat.text: That corner table wants another round and they look rough.
Come on, just one more, do not make a big deal of it.
What do you want me to do?

episodes.title: Bank Deposit Done
episodes.text: You lock the door after the last guests leave. You count the cash once more and seal the bag. You take the deposit to the night drop.

episodes.title: Morning Truck Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the yard while it is still cold. You walk around the truck and check the brakes, lights, tires, and emergency kit. You open the cab and check the gauges and safety gear.

trial.title: Find what is off
trial.scenario: You check the truck before you leave. The tires look good and the emergency kit is full. One brake light stays dark when you test the lights.
options: Left brake light is out
Tires have air
Emergency kit is stocked
trial.explain: You do not drive until the brake light works.

episodes.title: Checking Load Papers
episodes.text: You sit down in the office with the load papers. You read each line for weight, count, and signatures. You mark what is missing before you sign.

episodes.title: Tying Down Cargo
episodes.text: You stand on the dock beside the pallets. You pull covers over the load and throw ropes and chains across. You tighten the binders and set blocks so nothing can shift.

episodes.title: Talk About Dangerous Load
episodes.text: You meet your colleague by the placarded trailer to go over the safety steps.

choice.prompt: Your colleague asks if you can skip the full safety check to save time. What do you do?

options.label: Do the full check together
options.outcome: You both walk the placards and safety steps again. You leave ten minutes late with everything correct.

options.label: Skip it and roll
options.outcome: You pull out fast but you worry the whole drive. You have to stop later to fix the papers.

chat.text: This one has dangerous goods. Got the safety sheet?
Do we need the extra placards on the back?

episodes.title: Same Lot Check
episodes.text: You stop in the same rest lot as yesterday. You walk the same line and tug the same straps. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Loose Strap Problem
episodes.text: You stop and walk around the trailer. You see one chain hanging loose and the cover flapping. You stand there looking at the shifted block.

choice.prompt: The chain is loose on one corner and traffic is moving. What do you do first?

options.label: Pull fully off and re-secure
options.outcome: You park clear, set your brakes, and tighten the chain and binder. You check the rest of the load before you move.

options.label: Tighten it quick on the shoulder
options.outcome: You stay close to traffic and yank the binder tight. It holds for now but you still need a safe stop to check it right.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Monitors
episodes.text: You arrive before the first procedure starts. You sit down beside the anesthesiologist and check the EKG, arterial pressure, and heart rate. You make sure temperature and respiration readings are running.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You watch the EKG, direct arterial pressure, and temperature during the case. The EKG stays steady and temperature is steady, but direct arterial pressure starts falling fast.
options: Low arterial pressure
Steady EKG trace
Steady temperature
trial.explain: Falling arterial pressure needs help first because blood flow to the body drops.

episodes.title: Holding Anesthesia Steady
episodes.text: You stay at the bedside as the procedure starts. You watch the patient closely and help control anesthesia levels. You speak quietly with the anesthesiologist about small changes you see.

choice.prompt: The blood pressure drifts a little low while anesthesia runs. Do you speak up now or keep watching?

options.label: Speak up now
options.outcome: You tell the anesthesiologist what you see. You both adjust the level and keep watching the pressure together.

options.label: Watch one more minute
options.outcome: You keep your eyes on the monitor for another minute. You report the trend and stay ready to adjust.

episodes.title: Watching the Numbers
episodes.text: You sit and log temperature, respiration, blood pressure, and heart rate. You do the same checks you did yesterday. You will do the same checks tomorrow.

episodes.title: Giving Blood Fluids
episodes.text: You stay with the patient while blood and supportive fluids run. The anesthesiologist stays with you and talks through the rate.

chat.text: Keep the fluids running as ordered.
Tell me the pressure and heart rate every few minutes.

episodes.title: Heart Stops Suddenly
episodes.text: You see the heart rhythm fail on the monitor. You move into place and start CPR with the team. You get ready to give basic and advanced life support.

choice.prompt: The patient needs CPR and advanced support right now. What do you do first?

options.label: Start chest compressions
options.outcome: You start compressions right away. The team joins you and prepares advanced support drugs and equipment.

options.label: Call for the code cart
options.outcome: You call loudly for the cart and stay at the bedside. The team arrives and you start compressions together.

options.label: Take over the airway
options.outcome: You move to the head and open the airway. You help with ventilation while others start compressions.

episodes.title: Managing the Airway
episodes.text: You stand at the head of the bed near the end of the day. You help place the tube for tracheal intubation and check ventilary support. You watch the chest rise and listen for steady air movement.

episodes.title: Morning Delivery Check
episodes.text: You arrive before the cooks. You walk to the back door and look through the new supplies.

trial.title: Check the delivery
items: Put the good supplies away for the day
Walk around the delivery and work area
Look over supplies and equipment closely
Keep what meets standards and set aside what does not
trial.explain: You look first, then decide what meets standards before you put anything away.

episodes.title: Showing the Garnish
episodes.text: You stand beside two cooks at the prep table.

choice.prompt: The plate garnish is uneven and service is coming. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and show them again
options.outcome: You show the cut and plate once more. They redo the tray and it looks even.

options.label: Let them keep going as is
options.outcome: They finish the tray uneven. You have them fix it later before service.

chat.text: Chef, how thick should this garnish be?
Show me once more, I want to get it right.

episodes.title: Running the Line
episodes.text: You stand in the middle of the kitchen. You call out who does what for the lunch rush. You keep the cooks moving together.

episodes.title: Same Hand Wash Check
episodes.text: You walk the same loop as yesterday. You watch hands get washed and surfaces get wiped. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Dirty Station Found
episodes.text: You check the work area before dinner. You see sanitation standards are not being followed at one station.

choice.prompt: Dinner prep is starting and the station is not clean. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop work and clean it now
options.outcome: You pause that station and everyone cleans it. Prep starts late but clean.

options.label: Move prep to another area
options.outcome: You shift the cooks to a clean area. The dirty station waits to be cleaned after.

options.label: Remind them and keep prepping
options.outcome: You remind them of the standards and keep going. You watch closely while they work.

episodes.title: Ordering for Tomorrow
episodes.text: You sit down with the low stock list. You write the order for food and supplies for tomorrow. You send it off.

episodes.title: Morning Welcome Time
episodes.text: You arrive and open the classroom door. You sit on the rug and greet each child. You help with blocks and keep the start calm.

episodes.title: Talking With Parents
episodes.text: You sit down with a parent to discuss a behavior concern. You go over the classroom policy together.

choice.prompt: The parent asks what to do next about the behavior problem.

options.label: Agree on one shared rule
options.outcome: You write down the same calm-down words for home and school. You both use them starting today.

options.label: Ask to meet again next week
options.outcome: You set a time to check back in. You keep using the classroom plan until then.

chat.text: He has been hitting at home too. What do you do here?
We use the same calm-down words every time.
Can we try that at home as well?

episodes.title: Same Lunch Watch
episodes.text: You sit at the lunch table and watch the children eat. You note who finishes and who needs rest. Same as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Setting Learning Goals
episodes.text: You sit with staff around the small table. You review the learning goals for the term. You help set a simple policy to follow them.

episodes.title: Playground Dispute Now
episodes.text: You see two students arguing and one starts to cry. You step close and stop the play. You stay to help them work it out.

choice.prompt: Both children are upset and the group is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Calm them apart, then talk
options.outcome: You separate them for a few minutes to breathe. You bring them back and help them talk it through.

options.label: Bring the teacher in now
options.outcome: You call the teacher over to help settle them. You stay with the group while she talks with them.

options.label: Pause the game for all
options.outcome: You stop the game and have everyone sit. You restart play once the two are calm.

episodes.title: Meeting New Applicants
episodes.text: You sit down after the children leave to look at helpers. You talk with staff about who to bring in. You plan the next steps for hiring.

trial.title: Put hiring steps in order
items: Train new aides
Recruit applicants
Evaluate staff
Hire an aide
trial.explain: You recruit first, then hire, then train, then evaluate.

episodes.title: First Check Of Day
episodes.text: You greet your first patient and start your evaluation. You watch how they stand and walk. You test how their spine and joints move. You note what feels stiff or uneven.

trial.title: Steps of a diagnosis
items: You interpret the x-rays
You question the patient about symptoms
You review their health and medical history
You observe and examine the patient
trial.explain: You start with history before questions, exam, and x-rays.

episodes.title: New Patient History
episodes.text: You sit down with a new patient with a form on a clipboard. You start asking about past pain and illness.

choice.prompt: They mention the ladder fall quickly and move on. Do you pause on it now?

options.label: Ask more about the fall now
options.outcome: You ask when it happened and what hurt after. You write the details into their history.

options.label: Finish the rest of the form first
options.outcome: You keep going through the questions. You circle back to the fall before they leave.

chat.text: My neck has hurt for months now.
I fell off a ladder last year.
Do you need the name of my other doctor?

episodes.title: Hands On Adjustment
episodes.text: You have the patient lie still on the table. You place your hands on their lower back. You make a short controlled push to the joint. You check how it moves after.

episodes.title: Same Notes Again
episodes.text: You sit at your desk after lunch and update files. You type the same kinds of notes as yesterday. Same tomorrow. You save each one and close it.

episodes.title: X Ray Mismatch
episodes.text: You look at the morning x-rays next to the patient history. What the patient described does not match what you see. You pause before any adjustment.

choice.prompt: The history and the x-ray point different ways. What do you do next?

options.label: Re-examine and question again
options.outcome: You bring the patient back in and check the sore area again. You ask clear follow-up questions and note the answers.

options.label: Hold the adjustment and review
options.outcome: You do not adjust today. You review the history and x-ray side by side and record why you waited.

episodes.title: Closing The Files
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk at the end of the day. You open each case history from today. You check dates and details and save the final notes.

episodes.title: Checking Clean Vats
episodes.text: You arrive and walk the line of vats from last night's cleaning. You lean in and look for any sweet film left behind. You check that no fermentable residue remains before the day starts.

trial.title: Spot the dirty vat
trial.scenario: You inspect three vats after cleaning. Two look clear and dry inside. One still has a thin sticky film low on the wall.
options: The vat with sticky film still on the wall
A vat that looks clear and dry
A vat that looks clear and dry
trial.explain: Sticky film means fermentable residue was not removed.

episodes.title: Scrubbing Vats Clean
episodes.text: You clean and sterilize the vats and the processing area. You rinse, scrub, and rinse again. It is the same as yesterday and the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Starting Morning Cook
episodes.text: You set up the cooker for the first batch of the day. You weigh ingredients by the formula and start the mix. You stay by the machine as it cooks and blends.

choice.prompt: The mix starts thickening faster than the recipe describes. What do you do?

options.label: Lower the heat a little and keep watching
options.outcome: The mix steadies and keeps blending. You stay with it through the cycle.

options.label: Stop and restart the batch from the start
options.outcome: You empty the cooker and set it up again. The morning run starts over.

episodes.title: Testing Chocolate Sample
episodes.text: You pull a small sample from the batch. You test it for moisture and butter-fat content. You compare the reading to the target level.

episodes.title: Batch Won't Set Right
episodes.text: You test the afternoon batch and the moisture is still high. The reading is not where it needs to be. You keep the batch in process instead of moving it on.

choice.prompt: The sample is still off target. What do you do next?

options.label: Keep processing and test another sample
options.outcome: You let the batch run longer and test again. The next reading shows if it reached the level.

options.label: Move the batch on as it is
options.outcome: You send the batch forward without hitting the target. The test record shows the off reading.

episodes.title: Logging Batch Numbers
episodes.text: You sit down with the day's sheets. You record ingredients used, temperature, time cycle, and test results for each batch. You close out each food product batch before you leave.

episodes.title: Morning Steps Run
episodes.text: You arrive in the studio and call the dancers to places. You show the first eight counts slowly, then with music. You have them repeat it until the steps land together.

episodes.title: Finding The Rhythm
episodes.text: You sit at the front with three students who keep rushing the slow part. You clap the beat and have them walk it first, then turn the walk into movement. You ask them to show what the music feels like in their shoulders.

choice.prompt: One student stays stiff and off the beat. Do you keep working with her now?

options.label: Stay with her a few minutes
options.outcome: You stay beside her and clap softly while she tries again. She finds one bar and smiles a little.

options.label: Move the group on
options.outcome: You bring the group back together and have her follow the others. She watches and joins in when she can.

episodes.title: Same Posture Checks
episodes.text: You walk the line and check standing and knees again. Same corrections as yesterday about backs and weight. Same notes you will give tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cleaning The Effect
episodes.text: You run the middle section to fix the lift into the turn. You adjust arms and spacing so the shape reads clearly. You run it three times to hold the effect.

episodes.title: Stage Spacing Trouble
episodes.text: You are on stage for the run and two formations crowd together.

choice.prompt: The dancers are crowded in the second entrance. What do you change?

options.label: Widen the formation now
options.outcome: You move the marks wider and restage the entrance. The next run is clean and everyone can move safely.

options.label: Slow the entrance down
options.outcome: You keep the marks and reset the timing of the entrance. The dancers enter in two lines and stop crowding.

options.label: Cut one turn
options.outcome: You take out the turn that crowds the corner. The line moves through and finishes on time.

chat.text: We are bumping in the second entrance.
Do you want us to widen it?
We open soon, what do you want to change?

episodes.title: Writing Down Movement
episodes.text: You sit with your notebook after the run. You write down the changed steps, counts, and formations. You check your notes against what you just saw.

trial.title: Record the changes
items: Save the notes for the formations
Watch the run and note the steps
Write the counts and patterns
Check the notes against the movement
trial.explain: You watch first, then write it down and keep it.

episodes.title: Checking the Numbers
episodes.text: You arrive at the site trailer and sit down with your notebook. You work through load and grade numbers and water flow rates for today's pour.

trial.title: Order the calculation
items: Set the final design specifications
Measure the grade and water flow rates
Gather the load requirements for the site
Calculate the material stress factors
trial.explain: You gather requirements first, then measure and calculate before you set the specs.

episodes.title: Walking the Site
episodes.text: You put on your vest and walk the project site. You check the work against the design drawings and safety markings. You note where progress matches and where it does not.

episodes.title: Directing the Crew
episodes.text: You gather the crew near the foundation work to go over the next steps.

choice.prompt: The trucks are waiting and the crew looks to you. Where do you send them first?

options.label: Start on the north side now
options.outcome: You direct the pour to start north. The crew moves and the work stays on schedule for the morning.

options.label: Hold trucks and recheck the plan
options.outcome: You hold the trucks and walk the sequence again. The start is delayed but everyone is clear on the order.

chat.text: The concrete trucks are early. Do we start on the north side?
Hold them until you confirm the sequence. We need to stay on plan.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You sit with the same forms you filled out yesterday. You log the same measurements and initial the same boxes. Same as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Weak Soil Sample
episodes.text: You test a soil sample under the new footing and it feels soft. You run a second check and the strength still looks low for the foundation. You stop work in that spot while you decide what is safe.

choice.prompt: The footing area may not hold the load. What do you do?

options.label: Stop work there and retest
options.outcome: You keep everyone clear of the area and test again. You get a clear result to work from before anyone builds on it.

options.label: Shift work to another area
options.outcome: You move the crew to solid ground and mark the soft area off. The site keeps moving while you deal with the weak soil.

options.label: Ask for a design review
options.outcome: You call for a review of the foundation specs for that spot. Work waits there until the specs are confirmed safe.

episodes.title: Filing Compliance Notes
episodes.text: You sit back down in the trailer. You write up today's activities and note compliance with safety and environmental rules. You sign the sheet and file it for the record.

episodes.title: Picking Morning Supplies
episodes.text: You arrive at the supply closet with today's list. You match cleaner to linen, wood tables, and tile floors. You set out what the crew will use room by room.

episodes.title: Laundry Line Check
episodes.text: You walk through laundry and valet to start the shift.

chat.text: Washer two is running behind on sheets.
Dry cleaning rack is full too.
Keep them moving, rooms need linen by ten.

episodes.title: Same Rooms Again
episodes.text: You push the vacuum down the same hallway. You wipe the same sinks and empty the same bins. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Finished Work
episodes.text: You walk three finished rooms with your checklist. You look at beds, floors, and surfaces for missed spots. You mark what meets the standard and what does not.

trial.title: Find the Miss
trial.scenario: You inspect a finished room. The bed is made and the floor is mopped. The bathroom mirror is streaked and dusty.
options: The mirror needs rewiping to meet standard
The bed needs new linens
The floor needs mopping again
trial.explain: The mirror is the one detail that does not meet standard.

episodes.title: Missed Bathroom Detail
episodes.text: You recheck a room and the shower still has soap film. The guest check-in is soon and the room is not ready. You need to fix it now.

choice.prompt: The shower still fails standard and time is short. What do you do?

options.label: Stay and scrub it yourself
options.outcome: You scrub the shower and it passes. Your other checks run late.

options.label: Have the cleaner redo it now
options.outcome: The cleaner re-scrubs while you watch. The room passes after a second check.

episodes.title: Rooms Ready Call
episodes.text: You have your final list of clean, inspected rooms. You head to the front desk to pass them on. The clerk is waiting to assign arrivals.

choice.prompt: Two rooms are clean but you have not finished inspection. How do you report them?

options.label: Report only the inspected rooms ready
options.outcome: The clerk assigns those rooms. You inspect the other two and report them after.

options.label: Hold the full list until all are checked
options.outcome: You finish both inspections. You hand over the full list a little later.

episodes.title: Checking New Referrals
episodes.text: You arrive and open the list of new referrals. You sit down with three charts and compare each one to the study checklist. You mark who might fit and who clearly does not.

trial.title: Who Needs a Closer Look
trial.scenario: You review three records for a study that needs adults with no recent heart surgery. One record shows a surgery last month. Two others look clear and complete.
options: The record with surgery last month
One of the clear and complete records
All three records equally
trial.explain: That recent surgery breaks the study rules so you flag it first.

episodes.title: Explaining the Study
episodes.text: You sit down with a patient and a caregiver in a small visit room. You start to explain what the study will involve.

chat.text: So what will I actually have to do in this study?
You are doing great, take your time with the visit schedule.
And will you tell us what to expect after each visit?

episodes.title: Vitals and Heart Tracing
episodes.text: You bring the next subject back for protocol procedures. You interview them briefly, take vital signs, and set up the electrocardiogram. The tracing looks noisy and you are not sure it will count.

choice.prompt: The ECG tracing is noisy. What do you do now?

options.label: Adjust the leads and repeat the tracing now
options.outcome: You fix the leads and run it again. You get a clean tracing you can file.

options.label: Accept the noisy tracing and move on
options.outcome: You keep the visit moving. Later you have to redo it because it cannot be read.

episodes.title: Calling for Tomorrow
episodes.text: You sit at your desk with the schedule list. You call subjects to confirm appointments, procedures, and arrival times. It is the same calls as yesterday and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Screening Hits a Snag
episodes.text: You screen a potential subject and something in the history does not match the protocol. You pause the interview and check the notes. You need to decide before you go further.

choice.prompt: The history may fail eligibility. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and check with the nurse and records
options.outcome: You step out and review the records together. You get a clear yes or no before scheduling.

options.label: Enroll them now and sort it later
options.outcome: You book them in. You have to cancel later when the record shows they do not qualify.

options.label: Ask a few more screening questions first
options.outcome: You ask the extra questions and write down the answers. You still check with the team before deciding.

episodes.title: Writing Up the Day
episodes.text: You return to your desk to prepare study paperwork. You fill out protocol worksheets and update progress notes. You file everything so tomorrow starts clean.

episodes.title: Morning Network Check
episodes.text: You open your laptop and look at network operations. You see maintenance and an upgrade due this week. You plan the order to keep things running.

choice.prompt: One link needs maintenance now but an upgrade is also due. What do you do first?

options.label: Do the small maintenance now
options.outcome: You do the quick maintenance first. The network stays steady while you set up the upgrade.

options.label: Start the upgrade first
options.outcome: You hold the maintenance and start the upgrade. The old link runs a little longer until you switch over.

episodes.title: Daily Backup Run
episodes.text: You run the daily file backup. You add new files and delete old ones. You wait for it to finish. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Firewall Review Call
episodes.text: You join a video call about network security. Your colleague wants a clear recommendation on firewalls.

chat.text: Should we keep this firewall rule?
Last audit flagged extra open access.
What do you recommend we do?

episodes.title: Slow Link Fix
episodes.text: You see a slow section of the network. You trace the problem and test a fix. You put in a solution and watch it hold.

trial.title: Fix the slow link
items: Apply the fix to the network
Look at the checks to find the fault
Confirm the fix cleared the problem
Try a fix and see if it helps
trial.explain: You find it first, then test, then apply, then confirm.

episodes.title: Network Drop Hits
episodes.text: A part of the network drops in the afternoon. Messages come in about failed connections. You move to coordinate repairs.

choice.prompt: The network is down and repairs will take time. What do you coordinate first?

options.label: Shift traffic to the backup path
options.outcome: You move traffic to the backup path. Users get back on while repairs continue.

options.label: Keep traffic still and repair fast
options.outcome: You hold traffic and focus everyone on repair. The outage lasts until the repair is done.

options.label: Split the repair crew in two
options.outcome: You send one group to repair and one to set up backup. Both jobs move slower but move together.

episodes.title: Recovery Plan Draft
episodes.text: You open the disaster recovery plan. You write down steps for backup and restore. You save the draft for review.
